_readme: Every dataset the site uses must be listed here with its licence. Add a source here BEFORE writing an importer for it.

world-countries.name: world-countries by Mohammed Le Doze
world-countries.notes: Credit on the Data sources page. If we publish the combined database for download, it must also be ODbL.

wikidata.name: Wikidata
usedFor: head of state and government offices, anthem, motto (scripts/importers/wikidata-government.mjs)
how well known each country is, for quiz difficulty only (scripts/importers/wikidata-fame.mjs)
historical events: wars, battles, treaties, revolutions, historical states, with dates, places, participants, causes and effects (scripts/importers/wikidata-events.mjs)

world-bank.name: World Bank Open Data
usedFor: population, GDP per person, life expectancy since 1960 (scripts/importers/worldbank.mjs)
literacy, internet use, urban population, CO2 per person, forest cover, farmland and average rainfall, with world averages where the World Bank publishes one

member-lists.name: Official member lists of international organisations
member-lists.notes: Curated by hand in data/memberships.json, with each organisation's own member-list URL. Re-check when membership changes.
usedFor: memberships of the UN, EU, NATO, African Union and others

flag-icons.name: flag-icons by Panayiotis Lipiridis
flag-icons.notes: SVG flag images. National flags themselves are generally not copyrighted.

doNotUse._why: Copyrighted or licence-incompatible. Use them for inspiration only; never copy text, question lists or game designs.
list: CIA World Factbook text is public domain but check each page
Wikipedia article text (CC BY-SA: only with attribution and share-alike — prefer writing our own)
Any map tiles or images without an explicit licence
CShapes 2.0 historical borders (non-commercial licence; would block a paid tier)
Seshat Global History Databank (CC BY-NC-SA; non-commercial)
